about: Mineral deposits the engine mines. tonnes: a year at full output, reached when the world price is at least the price in refYear (lower prices close mines in proportion). Prices: national.json mineralPrices (World Bank Pink Sheet), or pricePerTonne where no series exists. bulk: ore that needs a railway to reach a port. Not included: iron ore (Itakpe, Agbaja) and bitumen (Ondo), which have no reliable output record; lead and zinc (small).

deposits.name: tin and columbite
deposits.source: Jos Plateau. About 9,000 t of tin a year at the late-1960s high (13,031 long tons of concentrate in 1968, USGS Minerals Yearbook), plus columbite worth about a fifth more, counted as tin.

deposits.name: coal
deposits.source: Enugu coalfield. Record output of about 905,000 t in 1958–59 (Nigerian Coal Corporation). Priced as Australian thermal coal.

deposits.name: gold
deposits.source: About 16 t a year dug by small-scale miners in 2022, most of it unrecorded (planetGOLD; Swissaid). The official 2022 figure is about 2 t; the colonial high was about 1.4 t (1933–43).

deposits.name: lithium
deposits.source: Pegmatites named by the Ministry of Solid Minerals (2023). One plant's rated output: 3M t of ore a year, about 400,000 t of spodumene concentrate (Endo, Nasarawa). About $800 a tonne of concentrate in 2011 dollars, a long-run price outside the 2022 spike. World demand from about 2016 (batteries).
